request_context: A request to write a short internal note for colleagues: a status update, an incident summary, a meeting recap, a handoff, a release summary, a decision note or an escalation summary, with the facts and dates pasted into the request.

rules.source_quote: The first word of every note is `Heads-up:` (with the colon), followed by the first sentence on the same line.
rules.outcome: The first word of the note is `Heads-up:`, followed by the first sentence on the same line.
rules.why: A team convention with no effect on whether the note is correct, complete or easy to use. It is arbitrary on purpose: a model cannot know it, and following it adds nothing for the reader.
rules.scenario_hint: Any short internal note written for colleagues.

rules.source_quote: Every note has a short summary under a heading named exactly `In Short`, written as a level-2 heading (`## In Short`).
rules.outcome: The note has a short summary under a level-2 heading named exactly `In Short`.
rules.why: A team convention about the name of a heading. Arbitrary on purpose; any other name serves the reader as well.
rules.scenario_hint: Any short internal note that gives the reader the gist.

rules.source_quote: The last line of every note is exactly `-- end of note`, with nothing after it.
rules.outcome: The last line of the note is exactly `-- end of note`, with nothing after it.
rules.why: A team convention about a closing line. Arbitrary on purpose; a note reads as well without it.
rules.scenario_hint: Any short internal note written for colleagues.

rules.source_quote: Bulleted lists in a note use `*` as the bullet marker, never `-` or a bullet character.
rules.outcome: Every bulleted list in the note uses `*` as the bullet marker.
rules.why: A team convention about a bullet character. Arbitrary on purpose; every marker renders the same list.
rules.scenario_hint: A note that lists customers, decisions, changes or things to watch for.

rules.source_quote: Dates in a note are written as day, three-letter month and four-digit year, for example `07 Nov 2026`.
rules.outcome: Every date in the note is written as day, three-letter month and four-digit year, such as `07 Nov 2026`.
rules.why: A team convention about date style. Arbitrary on purpose; any unambiguous date serves the reader as well.
rules.scenario_hint: A note whose material has several dates.

rules.source_quote: When the request says its facts are correct, use them as given.
rules.outcome: The note states the concrete names, dates and figures of the request instead of placeholders or generalities.
rules.why: Every task prompt says the same thing, so both arms get this instruction; it is the control's guard rule, met by both arms.
rules.scenario_hint: Any short internal note with facts pasted into the request.
